items.title: An explosion at a school in eastern Afghanistan kills 10, wounds 110
items.excerpt: Local officials said the blast appeared to have originated in a neighboring depot for mining explosives.

items.title: Sudan's lost generation: War is stealing the childhood of millions
items.excerpt: Three years of war have stolen childhood from millions of children in Sudan, leaving them displaced, hungry and fighting for survival instead of learning in a classroom.

items.title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
items.excerpt: The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.

items.title: As UN Secretary General's last day approaches, search for his replacement continues
items.excerpt: The UN Secretary General's term ends this year, but the big powers at the UN have been unable to agree on a replacement. UN watchers worry that there will be little time to get up to speed.

items.title: Strobe Talbott, former Time magazine reporter and deputy secretary of state, has died
items.excerpt: Strobe Talbott, a former Time magazine reporter who later served as deputy secretary of state under President Bill Clinton and then headed the Brookings Institution, died Thursday. He was 80.

items.title: Congo Ebola outbreak reaches 12,000 cases as some responders evacuate
items.excerpt: As the fast-moving outbreak continues to spread in eastern Congo, fighting between rebels and the army is disrupting efforts to contain the spread of the disease.

items.title: North Korea's Kim vows to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring Trump's overture
items.excerpt: Leader Kim Jong Un reportedly visited facilities that produce nuclear ingredients and called for building more nuclear weapons to cope with threats from the U.S. and South Korea.

items.title: Storms disrupt Thanksgiving travel. And, FCC violated ABC's free speech, judge says
items.excerpt: The East Coast's weather is a major concern this holiday, as it could lead to coastal flooding. And, the judge says the FCC can't punish ABC for satire Trump doesn't like.

items.title: How American Thanksgiving took root — and evolved — in Liberia
items.excerpt: The first settlers of Liberia were African Americans who brought along the holiday of Thanksgiving — which has evolved to reflect the history and identity of this new nation.

items.title: Army to detonate tons of lead azide after delays. And, Abrego Garcia leaves U.S.
items.excerpt: Authorities have evacuated a 5-mile radius to prepare to dispose of thousands of pounds of lead azide. And, after a nearly two-year legal battle, Kilmar Abrego Garcia's has voluntarily left the U.S.
